a.summary: The three pending-prune rows keep `# line 28` / `# line 37` / `# line 40` tags that point into the `DataEncoding` enum and `DATA_ENCODING_PARSER` lambda `0112d69` added, and the new section never says the tags are historical — the half of F3 that is still open.
a.failure_scenario: A reviewer follows `sava-core/config/pitest/README.md:63-64` ("The authoritative anchor is each row's `# line` tag in the CSV") to `responses-accepted.csv:2-4`, opens `JsonUtil.java` at lines 28, 37 and 40, and lands on `base58, base64, base64_zstd`, `return DataEncoding.base58;` and the lambda's closing `}` — code added *after* the rows were written, and belonging to `lambda$static$0`, not to `parseEncodedData` at all. The tags therefore read as a fresh re-anchoring onto new code rather than as pre-`0d68f02` history, which is exactly the misreading F3 reported. No sanctioned writer can fix this (`BaselineRetag` refreshes only matched rows, `sava-build/HARDENING.md:861-864`), so the README note is the only available remedy and it was not written.

b.summary: The commit removed F10's phantom `# shadowed default` documentation but left the identical phantom problem in the `# result identical routing` list two lines below it: the list documents six acceptances where `tx-accepted.csv` carries only three rows with that label, one of which has no row at all and another of which is filed under the wrong family.
b.failure_scenario: A maintainer triaging the tx baseline reads README:336-351 and expects six `# result identical routing` acceptances. `grep 'result identical routing' sava-core/config/pitest/tx-accepted.csv` returns exactly three rows: `InstructionRecord,extraAccounts` (line 27), `Transaction,createTx` (line 485), `TransactionSkeleton,deserializeSkeleton` (line 99). `grep 'TransactionRecord,sign' tx-accepted.csv` returns nothing, so the `TransactionRecord.sign` 154 bullet argues an acceptance that does not exist; only one of the two `Transaction.createTx` bullets (386 and 494) has a backing row; and the `TransactionSkeletonImpl.filterInstructions`/`filterInstructionsWithoutAccounts` bullet describes rows that actually carry `# array identity only` (tx-accepted.csv lines 22-23), whose argument is already written under its own heading at README:435-444. The maintainer either believes accepted survivors exist where none do, or hunts for a `TransactionRecord.sign` row that was killed or renamed long ago — exactly the failure F10 named, in the same file, in the section adjacent to the one this commit rewrote.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
